topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-02.1, when a real estate brokerage's advertising includes the name of an affiliated salesperson, associate broker, or team, how must the brokerage's trade name appear relative to that name?
choice_a: The trade name may be omitted if the licensee's own name is well known
choice_b: The trade name only needs to appear somewhere on the licensee's business card
choice_c: The trade name must be smaller so the individual agent's brand stands out
choice_d: The trade name must be equal to or greater than the licensee's or team's name in size and visibility
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(2) requires that advertising be done in the brokerage's licensed trade name, and that the trade name be equal to or greater than, in size and visibility, the name of any salesperson, associate broker, or team appearing in the ad. Choice D reverses the rule, and A and C ignore the requirement entirely.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under North Dakota advertising rules, what minimum information must every real estate advertisement include regardless of medium?
choice_a: Information on how the public can contact the real estate brokerage agency
choice_b: The designated broker's home address
choice_c: A statement of the commission percentage being charged
choice_d: The license number of every salesperson employed by the firm
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(3) requires that advertising include information on how the public can contact the real estate brokerage agency. It does not require the broker's home address, a stated commission rate, or every salesperson's license number.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A North Dakota broker wants to advertise, under her own name, a house that she personally owns. What must appear in the ad under NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(6)?
choice_a: Nothing extra is required since she owns the property
choice_b: The words "Owner/Licensed Broker" following her name
choice_c: A disclaimer that she is not acting as anyone's agent
choice_d: Her supervising broker's name, since all advertising must show a supervisor
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(6) requires a broker advertising personally owned property under the broker's own name to include the words "Owner/Licensed Broker" following the name; this applies even if the license is inactive. There is no supervising broker over a broker's own license, and a bare disclaimer of no agency does not satisfy the rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensed salesperson wants to sell her own home and advertise it herself. Per NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(7), what must follow her name in the advertisement?
choice_a: "For Sale By Owner" only, with no reference to her license
choice_b: Her employing broker's trade name in place of her own name
choice_c: "Owner/Licensed Salesperson"
choice_d: Nothing, because salespersons are exempt from advertising disclosure rules for their own property
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(7) requires a salesperson advertising personally owned property under the salesperson's own name to include "Owner/Licensed Salesperson" following the name, whether the license is active or inactive. Omitting the license disclosure or hiding behind "For Sale By Owner" language alone would not satisfy the rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(8), a "team" of licensees advertising together under a team name is prohibited from doing which of the following?
choice_a: Using a team name at all in advertising
choice_b: Listing individual team members' phone numbers
choice_c: Working together on the same transaction
choice_d: Advertising in any manner that suggests the team is an independent real estate brokerage firm
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-02.1(8) defines a team as licensees working under the same designated broker's supervision and expressly prohibits team advertising that suggests the team is an independent brokerage firm; the team is still bound by the same trade-name and contact requirements as any other advertising. Teams may use a team name and list members' contact information, and collaborating on transactions is part of the definition, not prohibited.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-05, a person who advertises or holds themselves out as a real estate broker without holding a North Dakota license has:
choice_a: Violated the license-required statute, which also makes them ineligible to collect any fee or commission for the activity
choice_b: Committed a purely civil matter with no criminal exposure
choice_c: Done nothing wrong as long as no sale actually closes
choice_d: Only violated the rule if they used the word "broker" specifically
explanation: NDCC 43-23-05 provides that a person may not act as, or advertise or assume to act as, a real estate broker or salesperson without a license, and is not entitled to collect any fee, compensation, or commission without having complied with the chapter. A violation of section 43-23-05 is also a class B misdemeanor under NDCC 43-23-17, so it is not merely civil, and the prohibition covers holding out generally, not just use of the specific word "broker."

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(r), a North Dakota broker is subject to discipline for which of the following?
choice_a: Hiring more salespersons than the broker personally trained
choice_b: Allowing an unlicensed salesperson to perform activity regulated under the chapter, carried on in the name of or under the authority of the broker
choice_c: Failing to attend the salesperson's initial licensing examination
choice_d: Allowing a licensed salesperson to work from a branch office
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(r) makes it a disciplinary ground for a broker to allow any unlicensed salesperson to do any act or engage in activity regulated by the chapter that is carried on in the broker's name or authority. Working from a properly licensed branch office is lawful, and neither the number of hires nor exam attendance is the statutory violation described.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A North Dakota salesperson decides to leave Broker A and join Broker B. Under NDCC 43-23-12(2), what happens if the salesperson changes brokers without giving the commission written notice?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as Broker B eventually notifies the commission
choice_b: The salesperson may continue working under Broker A's license until the next renewal cycle
choice_c: The salesperson's license is automatically canceled
choice_d: Only Broker A faces discipline; the salesperson's license remains valid
explanation: NDCC 43-23-12(2) provides that a change of broker by a licensed salesperson, without notice to the commission, automatically cancels that salesperson's license, and it is unlawful for the salesperson to perform licensed acts until a new license is reissued for the new broker.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-09, a broker associate who is affiliated with another broker but does not maintain an office under the broker associate's own name is subject to which requirement?
choice_a: The broker associate may act independently of the supervising broker at any time
choice_b: The broker associate is exempt from supervision because the associate already holds a broker's license
choice_c: The broker associate must open a branch office before doing any business
choice_d: The broker associate must not perform any real estate service without the full consent and knowledge of the supervising broker, who remains responsible for the associate's actions
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-09 treats a broker associate functionally like a salesperson for supervision purposes: the associate must not act independently or perform services without the supervising broker's consent, and the designated broker remains responsible for the associate's actions to the same extent as for an affiliated salesperson.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-14, when may a salesperson handle the closing of a real estate transaction?
choice_a: Only if authorized by the salesperson's broker, or under the direct supervision of the broker or a licensed officer or partner of the firm
choice_b: Never, closings must always be handled by an attorney
choice_c: Any time the salesperson feels confident doing so
choice_d: Only after five years of licensure
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-14 provides that a salesperson shall not handle a closing unless authorized by the salesperson's broker, or except under the direct supervision of the broker, a licensed officer, or a licensed partner of the corporation or partnership under whom the salesperson is licensed.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-21, what must a designated broker maintain regarding the types of agency relationships the firm engages in?
choice_a: Nothing in writing is required as long as agents understand it verbally
choice_b: A written company policy identifying and describing the types of agency relationships the agency may engage in, including procedures to prevent mishandling of information when representing both buyers and sellers
choice_c: A policy only if the firm has more than ten licensees
choice_d: A one-time filing with the commission at initial firm licensure, never updated
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-21 requires the designated broker to maintain a written company policy describing the agency relationships the firm may engage in, and, for firms representing both buyers and sellers, procedures addressing information-sharing safeguards, office space arrangement, and personal relationships among agents with adverse client interests. It also requires a written team policy and chronological team-membership records available to the commission on request.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-10, a newly licensed salesperson may begin performing real estate activities:
choice_a: Immediately upon passing the state licensing exam
choice_b: As soon as the salesperson pays the license fee, regardless of commission notification
choice_c: Only after the salesperson's broker receives notification of licensure from the commission
choice_d: After a 30-day waiting period from the exam date
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-10 states that a salesperson shall not commence work until the salesperson's broker receives notification of licensure from the commission. Passing the exam or paying the fee alone does not authorize the salesperson to begin practicing.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(q), a real estate salesperson who accepts a commission for licensed activity from someone other than the salesperson's employing broker has:
choice_a: Done nothing wrong if the payer is a cooperating broker
choice_b: Only violated a rule if the amount exceeds $500
choice_c: Acted properly as long as the employing broker is informed after the fact
choice_d: Committed a disciplinable act, since a salesperson may accept compensation for licensed acts only from the licensed broker under whom the salesperson is licensed
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(q) makes it a disciplinable act for a salesperson to accept a commission or valuable consideration for licensed activity from any person except the licensed broker under whom the salesperson is licensed. There is no dollar threshold, and after-the-fact disclosure to the broker does not cure the violation.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(l), which of the following is grounds for discipline of a North Dakota licensee?
choice_a: Paying compensation or commission in a real estate transaction to a person not licensed as a broker or salesperson under the chapter
choice_b: Paying a referral fee to another North Dakota-licensed broker
choice_c: Splitting a commission with the licensee's own employing broker
choice_d: Charging a flat fee instead of a percentage commission
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(l) lists paying compensation or commission connected to a real estate transaction to a person who is not a licensed broker or salesperson as a disciplinable act. Paying another licensed broker, splitting with one's own broker, and choosing a flat-fee structure are all lawful.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Regarding real estate commission rates, what is the North Dakota Real Estate Commission's official position under NDAC 70-02-01-18?
choice_a: It sets a statewide standard commission rate of six percent
choice_b: It neither recommends nor recognizes any agreement to fix or impose uniform rates of commission on any real estate transaction
choice_c: It caps commissions at a percentage tied to the sale price
choice_d: It requires all brokers in a county to charge the same rate
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-18 provides that the commission neither recommends nor recognizes any agreement to fix or impose uniform commission rates, reflecting that commissions in North Dakota are negotiable between broker and client rather than set by the commission or fixed by agreement among brokers.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Two North Dakota licensees have a dispute over how a commission should be split between them on a closed transaction. Under NDAC 70-02-01-17, what role does the real estate commission play?
choice_a: It will hold a formal disciplinary hearing to resolve the split
choice_b: It will order an even 50/50 split by default
choice_c: It is not authorized by law to consider or conduct hearings involving disputes over fees or commissions between licensees
choice_d: It refers the matter to PSI for binding arbitration
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-17 states plainly that the commission is not authorized by law, and will not consider or conduct hearings involving, disputes over fees or commissions between licensees; such disputes are left to civil resolution, not commission adjudication.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-05, what must every listing contract or sales contract in North Dakota state regarding brokerage compensation?
choice_a: Nothing; commission terms may remain entirely oral
choice_b: Only that a "reasonable" commission will be paid
choice_c: The commission rate charged by the largest brokerage in the market
choice_d: The amount of brokerage agreed, either as a specific dollar amount or a specific percentage
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-05 requires that all listing contracts or sales contracts state the amount of brokerage agreed to, expressed either as a specific amount or a specific percentage; a vague "reasonable commission" clause or an oral-only understanding does not satisfy this requirement.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-13(1) and NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(m), before a broker may purchase, for the broker's own account, property that the owner listed with that broker's office, the broker must:
choice_a: First make the broker's true position clearly known to the owner, with satisfactory written proof produced upon request
choice_b: Wait until the listing has expired
choice_c: Simply record the purchase with the county recorder
choice_d: Obtain approval from the commission before closing
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-13(1) requires a broker to first make the broker's true position (as a prospective buyer rather than a neutral listing broker) clearly known to the owner before buying listed property, directly or indirectly, and to produce satisfactory written proof of that disclosure on request. NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(m) separately makes failure to disclose such intention a disciplinable act. Waiting for expiration, recording the deed, or commission pre-approval do not substitute for the disclosure duty.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-13(3), a salesperson who wants to buy, for the salesperson's own account, property listed with the salesperson's own broker must:
choice_a: Get written permission from the buyer of a competing property
choice_b: First make the salesperson's true position clearly known to the owner, with satisfactory written proof produced on request, before buying or acquiring any interest
choice_c: Ask the commission to reassign the listing to another agent
choice_d: Nothing extra, since the duty applies only to brokers, not salespersons
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-13(3) extends the same personal-interest disclosure duty to salespersons: a salesperson may not buy, or acquire any interest in, property listed with the salesperson's broker, or take an option on it, without first making the salesperson's true position clearly known to the owner and producing satisfactory written proof on request. The duty is not limited to brokers.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-13(4), if a North Dakota broker sells a property in which the broker personally owns an interest, the broker must:
choice_a: Decline the transaction entirely
choice_b: Disclose the interest only if the purchaser specifically asks
choice_c: Make that ownership interest known to the purchaser
choice_d: Disclose the interest only after closing
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-13(4) requires a broker or salesperson who sells property in which they own an interest to make that interest known to the purchaser proactively, not only on request and not merely after the sale closes.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: For a real estate transaction involving residential property with one through four dwelling units, when must a licensee representing the seller make the written agency disclosure required by NDAC 70-02-03-15.1?
choice_a: At closing, along with the other closing documents
choice_b: Only if the buyer requests it in writing
choice_c: Within thirty days after the listing is signed
choice_d: At the first substantive contact, which for a seller representation means prior to the signing of the listing agreement
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(2)(a) defines "substantive contact" for seller representation as prior to the signing of a listing agreement, and requires the affirmative written disclosure of representation to be made at that point, not deferred to closing or made contingent on a buyer's request.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(3), which of the following may a licensee NOT disclose about a represented client without that client's informed, written consent?
choice_a: That the client being represented is willing to accept less than the asking or lease price
choice_b: The property's street address
choice_c: The general condition of the roof as observed during a showing
choice_d: The listing price stated in the MLS
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(3) protects specific bargaining-related confidences, including that the represented party will accept less than the asking price, will pay more than offered, the party's motivating factors, and alternative financing terms the party would accept, absent informed written consent. Public facts like the address, MLS list price, or an openly observable defect are not confidential bargaining information under this rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(6), a licensee's duty of confidentiality to a represented party does NOT excuse the licensee from:
choice_a: Disclosing the client's phone number to the other party
choice_b: Disclosing material defects in the property or facts that would constitute fraudulent misrepresentation if withheld
choice_c: Disclosing the client's motivating reason for selling
choice_d: Disclosing that the client would accept a lower price
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(6) expressly clarifies that the confidentiality provisions do not permit or require a licensee to keep confidential any material defects in the property known to the licensee, or facts whose concealment would constitute fraudulent misrepresentation. The other listed items are exactly the kind of bargaining confidences the rule protects, not overrides.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(7)(c), before a North Dakota licensee may act as a dual agent representing both the buyer and seller in the same transaction, what must occur?
choice_a: Only verbal consent from the party paying the commission is needed
choice_b: The commission must pre-approve the specific transaction
choice_c: The licensee must obtain the written consent of both parties through a written agreement that also sets forth who pays the licensee's fee
choice_d: Dual agency is banned outright in North Dakota
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(7)(c) requires that dual agency arise from a written agreement obtaining the consent of both parties, which must also set forth who is responsible for the licensee's fee, and requires the licensee to treat both parties honestly and impartially. Dual agency is not banned in North Dakota, but it does require this specific documented consent, not just verbal agreement from one side or commission pre-clearance.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-06, once a licensee obtains a proper acceptance of a written offer to purchase, what must the licensee promptly do?
choice_a: File the offer with the real estate commission
choice_b: Destroy the original offer once a new contract is drafted
choice_c: Wait until closing to release copies to either party
choice_d: Deliver true executed copies of the offer, signed by both seller and purchaser, to both the seller and the purchaser
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-06 requires the licensee to promptly tender every written offer to the seller and, upon obtaining proper acceptance, to promptly deliver true executed copies signed by both seller and purchaser to both parties -- not to withhold copies until closing, destroy the original, or file it with the commission.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(t), a North Dakota licensee is subject to discipline for:
choice_a: Failing to reduce a purchaser's offer to writing when the purchaser requests it be submitted to the seller, or failing to submit all offers received before the seller's written acceptance
choice_b: Refusing to write any offer below the listed price
choice_c: Presenting only the highest offer received to the seller
choice_d: Requiring earnest money to accompany every offer
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(t) makes it a disciplinable act for a licensee to fail to reduce a proposed purchaser's offer to writing when requested, or to fail to submit all offers received to the seller before the seller accepts one offer in writing and until the broker has knowledge of that acceptance -- meaning even lower or later-received offers generally must still be presented until an acceptance is final.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-06, if the seller makes material or extensive changes to the text of a purchaser's written offer, what should the licensee do?
choice_a: Ignore the changes and proceed with the original offer
choice_b: Make certain any changes are agreed to and initialed by the offeror, and if the changes are material or extensive, have the entire offer or contract rewritten
choice_c: Simply cross out the old terms without any signatures
choice_d: Have only the listing agent initial the changes
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-06 requires licensees to ensure that changes to the text of an offer are agreed to and initialed by the offeror before proceeding, and specifies that if the changes made are material or extensive, the entire offer or contract should be rewritten rather than patched with cross-outs or unilateral edits.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-09, a licensee who uses or knowingly permits the use of a loan application or other document that misstates facts to a lender so a purchaser can obtain a larger loan than the true sales price would allow has:
choice_a: Committed no violation as long as the loan is eventually repaid
choice_b: Only violated federal law, not North Dakota rules
choice_c: Engaged in a course of misconduct permitting suspension or revocation of the license, or assessment of fines
choice_d: Committed a minor infraction subject only to a warning letter
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-09 states that using, proposing, agreeing to, or knowingly permitting the use of a contract, earnest money agreement, loan application, mortgage, note, or other document not disclosed to the lender to enable a purchaser to obtain a larger loan or to qualify when they otherwise could not, constitutes a course of misconduct permitting license suspension, revocation, or fines -- a serious violation under North Dakota rule, independent of any federal exposure.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-14, a North Dakota broker or salesperson may accept a note or other nonnegotiable instrument as an earnest money deposit only if:
choice_a: The instrument is worth at least $1,000
choice_b: The commission has pre-approved the specific instrument
choice_c: It is never permitted under any circumstances
choice_d: The broker's or salesperson's principal has knowledge of and has given permission for it
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-14 provides that a broker or salesperson shall not accept a note, nonnegotiable instrument, or anything of value not readily negotiable as a deposit without the knowledge and permission of the broker's or salesperson's principal. There is no dollar minimum and no commission pre-approval mechanism for this.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: For residential property with one through four dwelling units, NDAC 70-02-03-04 requires a signed written listing agreement to be obtained from the seller before the property is advertised or offered for sale, and that agreement must include:
choice_a: The price, the commission to be paid, the signatures of all parties, and a definite expiration date
choice_b: Only the seller's signature; price and commission terms may be added later
choice_c: A clause requiring the seller to notify the broker before cancelling after the expiration date
choice_d: The buyer's name, even before a buyer is identified
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-04 requires a written listing agreement identifying the property, containing the price, the commission to be paid, the signatures of all parties, and a definite expiration date, obtained before advertising or offering the property for sale. It expressly forbids a provision requiring the seller to notify the broker of intent to cancel after the stated expiration date -- the opposite of choice C.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-04, if a listing is written as an "exclusive agency" or "exclusive right to sell" listing, what additional requirement applies?
choice_a: No extra requirement; any listing form works the same way
choice_b: The listing must clearly indicate that it is such an agreement, and a copy must be given to the owner at the time of signing
choice_c: The listing must be filed with the commission within 24 hours
choice_d: The commission percentage must be at least six percent
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-04 requires that an exclusive agency or exclusive right to sell listing clearly indicate in the agreement that it is such an arrangement, with a copy given to the owner at the time of signing -- there is no commission filing deadline or minimum commission percentage under North Dakota rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(n), a licensee is subject to discipline for:
choice_a: Including too many contingencies in a listing agreement
choice_b: Listing a property below its appraised value
choice_c: Failing to include a fixed date of expiration in a written listing agreement and failing to leave a copy of the agreement with the principal
choice_d: Renewing a listing agreement before its expiration date with the owner's consent
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(n) makes it a disciplinable act to fail to include a fixed expiration date in a written listing agreement and to fail to leave a copy of the agreement with the principal. The number of contingencies, listing price relative to appraisal, and a consensual pre-expiration renewal are not statutory violations.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: For residential property with one through four dwelling units, under NDAC 70-02-03-05.1, what must a licensee obtain from a buyer before performing any act as the buyer's representative?
choice_a: A verbal agreement is sufficient
choice_b: Nothing; buyer representation does not require a written agreement in North Dakota
choice_c: Only proof of buyer pre-qualification for financing
choice_d: A signed, written buyer's broker agreement including a definite expiration date, the amount of commission or other compensation, and a clear statement of the services to be provided
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-05.1 requires a signed written buyer's broker agreement before performing any act as a buyer's representative for one-to-four-family residential property, including a definite expiration date, the amount of commission or other compensation, and a clear statement of the services to be provided and the events triggering compensation.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-11, a North Dakota licensee generally may NOT negotiate a listing contract directly with an owner for compensation if the licensee knows the owner has:
choice_a: A written unexpired contract with another broker granting an exclusive right to sell or exclusive agency for that property
choice_b: A pending mortgage application with a lender
choice_c: Previously worked with a different agent more than a year ago
choice_d: An open house scheduled with another agent
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-11 prohibits a licensee from negotiating a listing (or, for a buyer, a purchase or exclusive-right-to-buy contract) directly with a party the licensee knows has an existing written, unexpired exclusive contract with another broker, unless the owner or buyer -- not the licensee -- initiates the contact and any new agreement does not take effect until the existing contract expires or is released.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-11(1), when is a broker's home considered a "branch office" requiring separate licensing?
choice_a: Whenever a broker works remotely more than half the time
choice_b: If the broker maintains a regular office elsewhere, the broker's home is not considered a branch office
choice_c: Anytime the broker meets a single client at home
choice_d: Only if the home is in a different city than the main office
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-11(1) provides that if a broker maintains a regular office, the broker's home is not considered a branch office; a branch office is defined as any additional office beyond the designated main office when more than one office is maintained.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-11(3), a broker opening a branch office must designate:
choice_a: A separate real estate commission member to oversee the branch
choice_b: Nothing; branch offices are self-supervising
choice_c: A branch office manager -- who may be the broker or another licensee -- to actively manage and supervise licensees working from that branch
choice_d: A local attorney to review all branch office contracts
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-11(3) requires the applicant broker to designate the broker or another licensee to act as branch office manager, responsible for actively managing the branch office and supervising the licensees working from it; the broker may serve as manager for all branch offices.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-11(4), if a broker changes the address of a branch office or changes who supervises it, the broker must notify the commission in writing within how many days?
choice_a: Immediately, with no grace period
choice_b: Thirty days
choice_c: Ninety days
choice_d: Five days
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-11(4) requires the applicant broker to notify the commission in writing of any change of address of a branch office or change of branch office supervisor within five days after the change occurs.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-11(7), a branch office's license must be displayed in the branch office or listed on the broker's website, and must bear:
choice_a: The address of the branch office and the name of the licensee designated to actively manage that branch
choice_b: Only the name of the real estate commission
choice_c: The broker's personal home address
choice_d: The purchase price of the most recent sale from that office
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-11(7) requires the branch license to be displayed in the branch office (or listed on the broker's website) bearing the branch office's address and the name of the licensee designated to actively manage that branch -- this is one of the three broker-only recordkeeping/display sub-areas (branch office/license display).

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-11(8), a branch office in North Dakota must be operated under:
choice_a: Any name the branch manager chooses, unrelated to the main office
choice_b: The same name as the principal office
choice_c: A name that includes the word "branch"
choice_d: No particular name requirement
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-11(8) requires that the branch office be operated under the identical name as the principal office, preventing brokers from operating branch locations under an unrelated or newly invented trade name.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-12, when two or more North Dakota brokers share the same physical office address, what is required of each broker?
choice_a: They may pool their trust accounts to simplify accounting
choice_b: Only one broker in the shared office needs a trust account
choice_c: Each broker must maintain all records and trust accounts separate from the other brokers, and operate under a business name that clearly identifies that broker individually within the group
choice_d: Sharing office space between brokers is prohibited outright
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-12 permits brokers to share office space at the same address, but requires each broker to keep all records and trust accounts separate from the other brokers and to operate under a business name that clearly identifies that broker as an individual broker within the group -- pooling trust accounts or relying on one shared account is exactly what the rule forbids.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(j), a North Dakota licensee is subject to discipline for refusing to show, sell, lease, or rent real estate to prospective renters, lessees, or purchasers because of:
choice_a: The prospective buyer's inability to provide proof of funds
choice_b: A prospective buyer's refusal to use the listing agent's preferred lender
choice_c: The property being outside the licensee's normal service area
choice_d: Race, color, national origin, religion, sex, age, physical or mental disability, or status with respect to marriage or public assistance
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(j) makes it a disciplinable act to refuse to show, sell, lease, or rent real estate because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, age, physical or mental disability, or status with respect to marriage or public assistance. Legitimate business reasons like inability to prove funds, lender-steering objections, or geographic service limits are not the discriminatory refusal the statute targets.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-10, before placing a "for sale" sign on a property, a licensee must:
choice_a: Obtain the consent of the owner or the owner's duly authorized agent
choice_b: Notify the county zoning office
choice_c: Wait until the listing agreement has been recorded
choice_d: Get sign-off from a neighboring property owner
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-10 provides that no signs shall be placed on any property for sale or lease without the consent of the owner or the owner's duly authorized agent -- there is no requirement to notify zoning offices, record the listing, or clear it with neighbors.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-08, what is a North Dakota licensee's obligation regarding legal advice?
choice_a: Licensees may draft binding legal opinions for clients as part of standard service
choice_b: No licensee should engage in activities that constitute the practice of law, and should recommend that title be examined and legal counsel obtained when the interest of either party requires it
choice_c: Licensees must always retain an attorney to close every transaction
choice_d: Legal advice may be given freely as long as the licensee has at least five years of experience
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-08 directs that no licensee should engage in activities constituting the practice of law, and should instead recommend that title be examined and legal counsel obtained when either party's interest requires it -- experience level does not authorize a licensee to give legal advice, and North Dakota does not mandate attorney-conducted closings for every transaction under this rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-20, if a prospective purchaser directly asks a North Dakota licensee whether a property may be "psychologically impacted" (for example, the site of a homicide), what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Refuse to answer, since psychologically impacted status is confidential
choice_b: State definitively that the property is not impacted, regardless of the facts
choice_c: Inquire of the owner whether there are facts or suspicions that the property is psychologically impacted, and advise the prospective purchaser of the owner's response, or that the owner refused to answer
choice_d: Refer the purchaser to the county sheriff's office for records
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-20 provides that while licensees are not required to volunteer that a property is psychologically impacted, if a prospective purchaser affirmatively asks, the licensee must inquire of the owner and advise the purchaser of the owner's response -- and if the owner refuses to answer, the purchaser must be told that the owner refused to answer.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-19 and 70-02-01-20, which of the following is specifically excluded from North Dakota's definition of a "psychologically impacted property" issue that a licensee must address if asked?
choice_a: The property being the site of a suicide
choice_b: The property being the site of a homicide
choice_c: The property being the site of another felony
choice_d: The fact or suspicion that a present or past occupant was infected with or died from HIV/AIDS or a similarly non-transmissible-through-occupancy disease
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-19 expressly carves HIV/AIDS status (or similar diseases medically determined highly unlikely to transmit through occupancy) out of the "psychologically impacted property" definition, distinguishing it from suicide, homicide, or other felony history, which do fall within the definition.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-07(9)(h), when may a North Dakota-licensed broker divide or share a real estate commission with a licensed broker in another state?
choice_a: Only if the out-of-state broker does not carry on any of the negotiations in North Dakota, whether by physically entering the state or communicating with the party electronically or otherwise
choice_b: Only if the out-of-state broker is licensed in all fifty states
choice_c: Commission sharing with out-of-state brokers is prohibited entirely
choice_d: Only for commercial, not residential, transactions
explanation: NDCC 43-23-07(9)(h), reiterated in NDAC 70-02-03-03, allows a North Dakota broker to divide or share a commission with a broker licensed in another state, provided the out-of-state broker does not carry on any of the negotiations on the referred client's behalf within North Dakota, whether by physically entering the state or communicating electronically. It is not limited to commercial transactions and does not require multistate licensure.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-12.1(6), if a real estate brokerage firm represents two or more sellers as clients who both want to offer competing properties for sale, what is the rule?
choice_a: The firm must drop one of the two listings immediately
choice_b: The firm and its licensees do not breach any duty to those clients by performing such services, even though the clients' interests compete, and must continue to honor agency duties to both
choice_c: The firm must disclose each seller's asking price to the other seller
choice_d: This scenario is entirely prohibited under North Dakota law
explanation: NDCC 43-23-12.1(6) allows a brokerage firm and its licensees to represent multiple sellers with competing properties without breaching any duty, so long as agency duties continue to be honored to each client as limited by that subsection -- it does not require dropping a listing or cross-disclosing confidential pricing information.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-12.1(5), if the SAME individual licensee has written buyer agency agreements with two or more buyers who want to make competing offers on the same property, what must that licensee do?
choice_a: Refuse to represent either buyer any further
choice_b: Automatically submit only the higher of the two offers
choice_c: Disclose to those competing buyer clients that a competing written offer has been submitted by another buyer client of that same licensee
choice_d: Nothing; no disclosure obligation exists in this scenario
explanation: NDCC 43-23-12.1(5) generally allows a brokerage firm to assist multiple competing buyer clients without breaching duty and without disclosing competing offers -- but when the same individual licensee has agreements with two or more buyers competing for the same property, that specific licensee must disclose the existence of the competing written offer to those buyer clients (though not, per NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(7)(b), the identity of the other buyer or the terms of that offer).

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(7)(a), what must be explained to a party who selects seller representation regarding subagents?
choice_a: A subagent automatically represents both the buyer and the seller equally
choice_b: Subagency does not exist under North Dakota law
choice_c: A subagent must work from the listing broker's own office
choice_d: A subagent may work in a different real estate office and can assist the buyer, but does not represent the buyer -- the subagent must place the owner's interest first
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(7)(a) explains that a subagent through the listing agency may work in a different real estate office, may assist the buyer, but does not represent the buyer -- the subagent, like the listing agent, must place the owner's interest first, and a buyer should not disclose anything to a subagent the buyer would not want the owner to know. North Dakota's chapter 43-23 expressly recognizes subagency as one form of agency relationship.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Which statement best reflects the North Dakota Real Estate Commission's own stated purpose under NDAC 70-02-01-01(2)?
choice_a: The commission's purpose includes safeguarding the public interest in real estate transactions and encouraging and requiring the maintenance of high standards of ethics and practices by all licensees doing business in North Dakota
choice_b: The commission exists solely to collect license renewal fees
choice_c: The commission exists to promote a specific brokerage's market share
choice_d: The commission's purpose is limited to administering the licensing exam
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-01(2) states the commission's purpose is to safeguard the public interest in real estate transactions, regulate licensing, and encourage and require the maintenance of high standards of ethics and practices by all real estate licensees doing business in North Dakota. This purpose clause is the closest thing North Dakota rule has to a codified ethics mandate, going well beyond fee collection or exam administration alone.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(v), if the commission determines a licensee's conduct does not meet the generally accepted standard of expertise, care, or professional ability expected of real estate brokers or salespersons, what is the commission's disciplinary authority under that specific subdivision limited to?
choice_a: Immediate license revocation with no hearing
choice_b: A letter of reprimand to the offending licensee
choice_c: A mandatory five-thousand-dollar fine
choice_d: Criminal referral to the state's attorney
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(v) provides that any conduct falling below the generally accepted standard of expertise, care, or professional ability -- as distinct from the more serious violations elsewhere in the statute -- limits the commission's disciplinary measures under that specific subdivision to issuance of a letter of reprimand, not revocation, a mandatory fine, or criminal referral.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(u), a North Dakota licensee's conduct constituting dishonesty or fraudulent conduct is a ground for discipline:
choice_a: Only if it occurs during a licensed transaction
choice_b: Only if a criminal conviction results first
choice_c: Whether the conduct is of the same or a different character than the specifically listed violations, and whether it arises within or outside the pursuit of the person's licensed privilege
choice_d: Only if the conduct harms another licensee, not a member of the public
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(u) is a broad catch-all reaching "any other conduct, whether of the same or of a different character than specified in this subsection, which constitutes dishonesty or fraudulent conduct, whether arising within or without the pursuit of that person's licensed privilege" -- meaning it can reach conduct outside licensed transactions and does not require a prior criminal conviction.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-19, as a condition of licensure North Dakota real estate brokers and salespersons (except those holding inactive licenses) are required to:
choice_a: Join the state's REALTOR association
choice_b: Post a surety bond with the secretary of state
choice_c: Complete a separate ethics certification exam every two years
choice_d: Carry errors and omissions insurance covering all activities contemplated under chapter 43-23
explanation: NDCC 43-23-19 directs the real estate commission to adopt rules requiring, as a condition of licensure, that all real estate salespersons and brokers (other than those with inactive licenses) carry errors and omissions insurance covering activities under the chapter -- a professional-standards safeguard tied to licensure, not a separate ethics exam, association membership, or bond requirement.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-14.1, every North Dakota broker must maintain trust funds belonging to others in what type of account?
choice_a: A separate, noninterest-bearing trust account, designated as such, in a federally insured financial institution in North Dakota
choice_b: An interest-bearing money market account in any state
choice_c: The broker's personal checking account, clearly labeled
choice_d: A joint account shared with the seller's attorney
explanation: NDCC 43-23-14.1 requires every broker to maintain, in the broker's or firm's name, a separate, noninterest-bearing trust account designated as such, in a federally insured financial institution located in North Dakota, into which the broker must immediately place all funds belonging to others as a demand deposit.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(a), what must the name of a North Dakota broker's separate trust account identify it as?
choice_a: "Operating account" or "business account"
choice_b: "Trust account" or "escrow account"
choice_c: The broker's personal legal name only
choice_d: "Client fund holding"
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(a) requires that the name of the broker's separate account be identified by the words "trust account" or "escrow account," clearly distinguishing it from an operating or personal account.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-14.1 and NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(d), a broker's general prohibition against commingling personal funds in the trust account has what specific exception?
choice_a: A broker may keep unlimited personal funds as long as they are tracked in a spreadsheet
choice_b: There is no exception; commingling is prohibited under all circumstances
choice_c: A broker may deposit and keep up to $500 of personal funds in the account, specifically identified, to cover service charges related to the trust account
choice_d: A broker may keep personal funds equal to one month's rent for the office
explanation: Both NDCC 43-23-14.1 and NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(d) allow a narrow exception to the commingling prohibition: a broker may deposit and keep a sum not to exceed $500 of the broker's own personal funds in the trust account, specifically identified and deposited solely to cover bank service charges related to the account.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(s) and NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(f), within how long after receipt must real estate trust money generally be deposited into the broker's trust account?
choice_a: Seventy-two hours
choice_b: By the end of the calendar month
choice_c: At the closing of the transaction
choice_d: Twenty-four hours of receipt by the broker or the salesperson, unless the purchase contract provides otherwise -- or the next business day if received before a day the depository is closed
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(s) and NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(f) both require trust money to be deposited within twenty-four hours of receipt by the broker or the broker's salesperson (unless the purchase contract provides otherwise), with a next-business-day extension if the money is received on a day before a holiday or other closure of the depository.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(f), if earnest money is wired by the buyer to the broker's trust account (or to a nonbroker third party), what must the broker maintain in the broker's office?
choice_a: A complete record of all moneys transferred, including the buyer's initial contact request for the wire and confirmation of completion of the transfer
choice_b: Nothing extra beyond the standard bank statement
choice_c: Only the buyer's bank routing number
choice_d: A notarized affidavit from the buyer's bank president
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(f) requires that when trust money is wired to either the broker's trust account or a nonbroker third party, the broker maintain a complete record of all moneys transferred, including the initial contact request for the wire from the buyer to the buyer's financial institution, and confirmation of completion of the transfer.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(f), if a buyer mails earnest money to the broker or a nonbroker third party rather than delivering it in person, what must the broker retain?
choice_a: Nothing; mailed deposits are exempt from timing rules
choice_b: The envelope containing the postmark, to establish the date the money was sent
choice_c: A copy of the buyer's driver's license
choice_d: A written apology letter from the buyer for the delay
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(1)(f) requires that when earnest money is mailed, the broker retain the postmarked envelope to establish the date the money was sent, which matters for determining compliance with the 24-hour (or next-business-day) deposit deadline.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(2)(c), when is a North Dakota broker entitled to any part of the earnest money as the broker's commission or fee?
choice_a: As soon as the earnest money is deposited into the trust account
choice_b: Immediately upon the seller's verbal acceptance of the offer
choice_c: Not until the transaction has been consummated or terminated
choice_d: Whenever the broker decides the deal is likely to close
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(2)(c) provides that a broker is not entitled to any part of the earnest money or other moneys received in connection with a transaction, as part or all of the broker's commission or fee, until the transaction has been consummated or terminated -- deposit into trust or a verbal acceptance does not by itself entitle the broker to draw against those funds.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(2)(d), an earnest money deposit that has remained unclaimed for more than how long after it becomes payable or distributable is presumed abandoned and must be reported to the state's unclaimed property division?
choice_a: Six months
choice_b: Ten years
choice_c: One year
choice_d: Three years
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(2)(d) provides that abandoned deposits in a broker's trust account are subject to North Dakota's unclaimed property law (NDCC ch. 47-30.1), and a deposit unclaimed for more than three years after becoming payable or distributable is presumed abandoned and must be reported and delivered to the administrator of the unclaimed property division. Earnest money is treated as payable or distributable as of the closing date or the date of cancellation of the purchase agreement.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-14.1, a broker who does not accept trust funds in any real estate brokerage transaction may:
choice_a: Apply for and receive a waiver from the real estate commission excusing the broker from maintaining a designated trust account, but must open one if the broker later receives trust funds
choice_b: Never be required to maintain a trust account, permanently and automatically
choice_c: Only avoid a trust account by operating as a sole proprietor
choice_d: Deposit all funds into the state treasury instead
explanation: NDCC 43-23-14.1 allows a broker who does not accept trust funds to apply for and receive a waiver from the real estate commission, relieving the broker of the trust account requirement -- but if that broker later receives trust funds in a transaction, the broker must then open a designated trust account and deposit the funds as required. The exemption is not automatic or permanent; it requires an application and waiver.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(g), a North Dakota broker must keep permanent records of all funds and property of others received by the broker for not less than:
choice_a: Two years from the date of receipt
choice_b: Six years from the date of receipt
choice_c: Ten years from the date of receipt
choice_d: One year from the closing date only
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(g) requires every broker to keep permanent records of all funds and property of others received by the broker for not less than six years from the date of receipt of the funds or property.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(d), a broker's trust account journal recording funds received must include which specific information for each entry?
choice_a: Only the total year-to-date balance
choice_b: The buyer's social security number
choice_c: The date, the name of the party giving the money, the property address, and the amount, plus a running balance shown after each entry
choice_d: Nothing beyond the deposit slip itself
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(d) requires the trust account journal to show the chronological sequence of receipts and disbursements: for funds received, the date, the name of the paying party, the property address, and the amount; for disbursements, the date, payee, and amount; and a running balance after each entry.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(e), what distinguishes the trust account "ledger" from the trust account "journal"?
choice_a: There is no meaningful difference; they are the same document under a different name
choice_b: The ledger is optional, while the journal is mandatory
choice_c: The ledger only tracks broker income, not client funds
choice_d: The ledger shows the receipts and disbursements as they affect a single, particular transaction between buyer and seller, while the journal shows the overall chronological sequence of all funds
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(d) and (e) distinguish the two records: the journal is the chronological, account-wide sequence of receipts and disbursements with a running balance, while the ledger is a per-transaction record showing receipts and disbursements as they affect a single transaction between a particular buyer and seller, including both parties' names, dates, and amounts. Both records are mandatory.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(f), how often must a North Dakota broker's trust account be reconciled?
choice_a: Monthly, except in a month where there was no account activity
choice_b: Annually, at license renewal time
choice_c: Only when the commission requests an audit
choice_d: Weekly, without exception
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(f) requires the trust account to be reconciled monthly, except in a month where there had been no activity in the account -- reconciliation is not left to an annual cycle or triggered only by a commission audit request.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(c), trust account checks must be numbered, and what else does the rule require regarding those checks?
choice_a: Voided checks may be shredded immediately
choice_b: All voided checks must be retained, and the checks must denote the broker's business name, address, and be designated as "real estate trust account"
choice_c: Checks need only show the broker's personal name
choice_d: Checks must be pre-signed in blank by the broker for staff convenience
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(c) requires trust account checks to be numbered, with all voided checks retained, and the checks themselves must denote the broker's business name and address and be designated as "real estate trust account" -- shredding voided checks or pre-signing blank checks would undermine the recordkeeping and internal-control purpose of the rule.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(o) and NDAC 70-02-03-07, in every real estate sales transaction, a broker representing a party must:
choice_a: Provide a closing statement only if the client specifically requests one in writing
choice_b: Discard closing statements once the deal has closed to protect client privacy
choice_c: Deliver a complete detailed closing statement showing all receipts and disbursements handled for the represented party, and retain true copies of that statement in the broker's files
choice_d: Provide only a verbal summary of receipts and disbursements
explanation: NDCC 43-23-11.1(1)(o) makes it a disciplinable act for a broker to fail to deliver a complete detailed closing statement to the party or parties the broker represents, showing all receipts and disbursements handled by the broker, and to fail to retain true copies of the statement in the broker's files. NDAC 70-02-03-07 extends this duty even when a third party (attorney, bank, etc.) handles the actual closing.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(a), what must a bank deposit slip for trust funds show?
choice_a: Only the total balance of the trust account
choice_b: Only the depositor's signature
choice_c: The broker's annual gross commission income
choice_d: The date of deposit, amount, source of the money, and where deposited
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(3)(a) requires that bank deposit slips for trust funds show the date of deposit, the amount, the source of the money, and where it was deposited -- a running account total or annual income figures do not satisfy this per-deposit documentation requirement.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(2), when a licensee makes the required written agency disclosure to a party, what must the broker do with that disclosure once it is offered and, where obtained, signed?
choice_a: Retain true copies of the disclosure form in the broker's file
choice_b: Discard it once the transaction closes
choice_c: Send it only to the real estate commission, not keep an office copy
choice_d: Nothing further is required once it is verbally explained
explanation: NDAC 70-02-03-15.1(2) requires that the written agency disclosure be represented by a separate document offered to the party for signature, and that true copies of the disclosure form be retained in the broker's file -- part of the broker's overall recordkeeping obligations, not something to discard post-closing or send only to the commission.

topic: Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under NDAC 70-02-01-15(2)(a), from what source may a broker pay the broker's own personal debts out of the trust account?
choice_a: Personal debts may always be paid from the trust account as long as they are logged
choice_b: The broker may withdraw earned commissions payable to the broker, or make withdrawals on behalf of the trust account's beneficiaries, but may not otherwise pay personal indebtedness from the trust account
choice_c: Personal debts may be paid from the trust account up to the $500 service-charge allowance
choice_d: There is no restriction on paying personal debts from the trust account
explanation: NDAC 70-02-01-15(2)(a) provides that no payments of the broker's personal indebtedness shall be made from the trust account other than a withdrawal of earned commissions payable to the broker, or withdrawals made on behalf of the beneficiaries of the trust account -- the $500 service-charge allowance under 70-02-01-15(1)(d) is a separate, narrower provision for bank service charges, not general personal debt.
